text:
anya (Eng): Quick heads-up — landing the HTTP/2 streaming multiplex rewrite (v3) to canary earlier today. Early numbers look solid for short-chat workloads (<256 tokens): p50 -30%, p95 -22%, p99 -28% and approx 12% infra cost drop for hosted traffic. :tada:

sahil (runtime): Nice! TL;DR on what changed?

anya (Eng): We changed the streaming layer to use a persistent HTTP/2 stream per client session and multiplex response chunks instead of spinning up short-lived connections per request. Also rewrote the streamer to avoid blocking syscall paths during flush, which cut CPU sys time.

zach (SRE): Where are the canary numbers? I want to check tail latency and connection churn.

deploy-bot: [canary] deploy v3-stream-mux -> canary cluster: success on 8/8 hosts. Canary window: 45m.

observability-bot: Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/streaming/streaming-mux-v3
 - metric: runtime.http2.stream_mux.p99_latency
 - canary cohort: canary-2026-03-02-v3

anya (Eng): Snapshot from the canary graphs (short-chat cohort):
 - p50: 24ms -> 17ms (-29%)
 - p95: 120ms -> 94ms (-21.6%)
 - p99: 450ms -> 324ms (-28%)
 - CPU sys% per request down ~18%
 - active connections per host down ~40%
Estimated hosted unit cost improvement: ~12% due to reduced CPU and fewer TCP handshakes.

maria (Product): Any customer-visible regressions? How about long-form/streaming large responses?

sahil (runtime): No regressions for long responses in canary — we keep the old path for >1024 token streams as a fallback for now. The mux path optimizes small interactive sessions.

zach (SRE): Did we see any increase in memory usage or file descriptor counts?

anya (Eng): FD counts per process increased a bit (expected) but well within headroom. Memory change negligible (+<2%). We added an FD pool and watcher in the runtime; it auto-evicts idle streams after 60s.

sahil (runtime): Rollout plan:
```
- step 0: canary 8 hosts (done)
- step 1: 10% traffic (24h), monitor p99 and connection churn
- step 2: 50% traffic (24h), apply auto-throttle if p99 regresses
- step 3: full rollout (gradual, 6h waves)
```
Enable flags: `runtime.stream_mux_v3=true` `runtime.stream_mux_fallback_threshold=1024`

observability-bot: Alert rules created:
 - stream_mux_v3_p99_regress (p99 > baseline * 1.12 for 10m)
 - stream_mux_fd_high (fds > 85% for 5m)

maria (Product): Please add a short bullet for customer comms — this looks like a reliability + latency win for chat features.

anya (Eng): Will draft a one-paragraph note for product updates and status page blurb.

zach (SRE): Any action items for oncall if it goes sideways?

anya (Eng): Yes — rollback playbook is just `runtime.stream_mux_v3=false` + restart routing pods. Document is at: https://confluence.redwood/d/streaming/mux-rollout-playbook

sahil (runtime): Also FYI: small perf testing snippet if you want to repro locally:
```
# run local mux harness (go)
go run ./cmd/stream-harness -endpoint https://staging.stream.redwood -parallel 200 -max_tokens 128
```

anya (Eng): Thanks team. Next steps: alert watch for 24h during 10% traffic ramp, PRD note to customers, and postmortem only if we see >5% user-facing errors. Huge thanks to @sahil and infra folks for the rewrite. :rocket:
